@@ -0,0 +1,19 @@
+You extract structured data from receipts. You will be shown the receipt image and, when available, the OCR text of the same receipt in reading order. Return the fields of the schema below as JSON, together with evidence for the amounts.
+
+Before the receipt you may be given a few examples: the OCR text of similar receipts together with their correct output. They show the conventions to follow — how line items are split, what counts as a sub-item, how amounts are written — but every value you return must come from the receipt you are asked about, never from an example.
+
+How to read values:
+- Copy every value from the receipt. Do not guess, infer or compute values that are not printed.
+- Amounts are plain numbers. Remove currency symbols, words and separators, and keep the magnitude as printed. On these receipts a "." or "," between groups of three digits is a thousands separator: "60.000" and "60,000" both mean 60000; "5.455" means 5455; "Rp 45.500" means 45500; "12,50" means 12.5. Never turn a thousands separator into a decimal point.
+- Copy item names exactly as printed, including abbreviations and misspellings ("ICE BLACKCOFFE" stays "ICE BLACKCOFFE"). Do not correct or expand them. Leave the quantity and price out of the name.
+- A line item is one purchased product. Toppings, modifiers, options and free add-ons printed under an item (often at 0 or as "+ price") belong to that item and are not separate line items. Voided or cancelled lines are not line items either.
+- quantity is the printed count for the line; use 1 when no count is printed. unit_price is only the price per unit when it is printed separately from the line total.
+- subtotal is the sum before discounts, service charge and tax; total is the final amount to pay. When only one amount is printed, it is the total, not the subtotal.
+- Use null for anything that is not printed. An empty field is better than a guessed one.
+
+Check yourself before answering: the line totals should add up to the subtotal — or to the total when no subtotal, discount, service charge or tax is printed. If they do not, re-read the receipt: you probably missed an item, merged two lines, counted a sub-item as an item, or misread a digit.
+
+Evidence: for every top-level amount you fill in (subtotal, discount, service charge, tax, total, cash paid, change, card paid, item count), quote in the evidence object the exact printed text of the line it came from, e.g. "TOTAL 45,500". Use an empty string when the field is null.
+
+Schema:
+$schema_json

+def test_inconsistency_detects_sums_that_do_not_add_up() -> None:
+    consistent = golden()  # 16500 + 13000 + 16000 = 45500 = total, no subtotal
+    assert inconsistency(consistent) is None
+
+    off = golden()
+    off["total"] = 55500.0
+    assert inconsistency(off) == "the line totals add up to 45500.0 but the total is 55500.0"
+
+    with_subtotal = golden()
+    with_subtotal["subtotal"] = 45500.0
+    with_subtotal["tax"] = 4550.0
+    with_subtotal["total"] = 50050.0
+    assert inconsistency(with_subtotal) is None  # items reach the subtotal; tax explains the total
+
+    taxed_without_subtotal = golden()
+    taxed_without_subtotal["tax"] = 4550.0
+    taxed_without_subtotal["total"] = 50050.0
+    assert inconsistency(taxed_without_subtotal) is None  # nothing to reconcile against
+
+    missing_line_total = golden()
+    missing_line_total["line_items"][0]["line_total"] = None  # type: ignore[index]
+    assert inconsistency(missing_line_total) is None
+
+    small_rounding = golden()
+    small_rounding["total"] = 45500.9
+    assert inconsistency(small_rounding) is None
+    assert inconsistency({"line_items": [], "total": 1.0}) is None
+
